author: Nayan Seth
description:
China said on Thursday that the recent government approval allowing American bank card payment giant Visa to operate in the country was the “direct outcome” of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit to the United States last month.
“The Visa card was granted permission to establish a banking card clearing institution,” said Qiu Wenxing, the Deputy Chief of Mission at the Chinese embassy in Washington.
“It is a direct outcome of the presidential summit.”
Visa received administrative approval...
title: Visa’s China approval a ‘direct outcome’ of Trump-Xi summit, Beijing says

author: Teresa Elena Frontado
description:
White House press secretary Katie Zacharia has acknowledged that she never passed a bar exam, days after telling reporters she had passed one “when I moved to China”.
In an interview with the conservative commentator Jack Posobiec on right-wing streaming channel Real America’s Voice on Thursday, Zacharia said she sat the California bar exam after graduating from Pepperdine University’s law school in 2011 but did not pass.
She said the results were “somewhat inconsequential, because I knew I...
title: Trump press secretary Katie Zacharia never passed bar exam, wrongly claims China has none

author: Igor Patrick
description:
Trade between Brazil and China reached a record US$143 billion in the first nine months of the year, driven by Brazilian oil sales that surged after the war on Iran disrupted Gulf supply, according to a report by the Brazil-China Business Council.
Brazilian exports to China rose 12 per cent to US$84.7 billion between January and September, while imports from China grew 9.9 per cent to US$58.6 billion, the council said in its quarterly analysis of government data. The resulting US$26.1 billion...
title: China bought half of Brazil's oil exports as Iran war shut Hormuz, driving sales to record

author: Finbarr Bermingham
description:
Chemicals and industrial machinery were identified as the top priority industries the EU needs to shield against Chinese imports during a meeting between the EU’s top leaders in Brussels on Thursday.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen told the bloc’s 27 member states that the EU should consider quickly introducing safeguard measures, which can involve import quotas and tariffs, to shield these sectors from a wave of cut-price alternatives from China, according to people familiar...
title: Chinese chemicals and machinery in EU crosshairs as leaders back more trade curbs

author: Dannie Peng
description:
Leading life scientist Wu Jun, who recently left the United States to return to his homeland, believes many of the world’s top embryo researchers are now working in China.
Wu, well known for his stem cell research, particularly related to the stem cell-derived embryo model, is speaking in an office at Westlake University, in Hangzhou in the eastern province of Zhejiang. Some of his belongings remain in bags placed haphazardly on a nearby cabinet, waiting to be unpacked.
“This is just a temporary...
title: China is a beacon of global embryo research, says scientist on return from US to lead lab

author: SCMP
description:
We have selected seven of the most interesting and important news stories covering US-China relations from the past few weeks. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. US investigates 9 universities over alleged visa fraud, with focus on China

The Trump administration launched an investigation into nine US universities over alleged J-1 visa fraud, with officials raising concerns about Chinese scholars and the Chinese government.
Read the full story...
title: Blast simulation, university probes, robotics fine, AI spies: 7 US-China relations reads

author: Peter T. C. Chang
description:
When US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping meet again in Shenzhen next month, and then in Miami in December, the world will watch for signs of progress on trade, technology, security and other contentious issues. Such high-level diplomacy is indispensable.
But the future of the US-China relationship also depends on something less visible: whether their people, especially the young, can still understand one another.
As Washington and Beijing navigate intensifying strategic...
title: Young Americans are key for the US to better understand China

author: Victoria Bela
description:
A China-led international team has reported a new pre-earthquake phenomenon that has shown strong predictive potential for major earthquakes since 2022 with minimal failures.
The anomalous seismic, magnetic and ionospheric resonance signals they observed – termed “seismo-ripples” by the researchers – are ringlike disturbance patterns triggered before earthquakes happen.
Their findings challenge the long-standing scientific belief that these events are unpredictable, opening up a promising new...
title: China-led team hits 83% success rate anticipating earthquakes in ‘seismo-ripples’ study

author: Laura Zhou
description:
The US wants to “compete” in resource-rich Central Asia, a senior American official has said as Secretary of State Marco Rubio prepares to head to a region of growing Chinese influence.
In New Delhi on Thursday, US ambassador to India Sergio Gor said this weekend’s C5+1 ministerial meeting between the five Central Asian countries and the US in Uzbekistan would be an opportunity to “showcase American ingenuity, American technology”.
Rubio would be joined by representatives from more than 200...
title: US wants to ‘compete’ in Central Asia, ambassador says ahead of Rubio visit

author: Carol Yang
description:
China’s premier has reaffirmed his country’s support for North Korea and its leader during the much-delayed opening of a new bridge between the neighbours.
In a taped speech to the opening ceremony on the New Yalu River Bridge on Thursday, Premier Li Qiang said the link was a landmark in Chinese-North Korean friendship.
Li said the bridge would promote economic and trade ties, expand personnel exchanges and tighten the bond between the two peoples, according to state news agency Xinhua.
The...
title: China keen to strengthen North Korea trade ties with New Yalu River Bridge opening

author: Brian Rhoads,Raymond Ma
description:
China and the United States are in regular talks about artificial intelligence (AI) as they seek to firm up plans for an incident “hotline” and develop a formalised dialogue process ahead of a presidential summit next month.
The two sides aim to agree on a basic framework for addressing AI incidents before Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump meet on the sidelines of the annual Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) leaders’ meeting in Shenzhen, the South China Morning...
title: China, US discuss AI as chip stock rout hits Asian markets

author: Orange Wang
description:
The foreign ministers of China and Russia have discussed their relations with the United States, paving the ground for a possible meeting between their respective leaders at next month’s Apec summit in Shenzhen.
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and his Russian counterpart, Sergey Lavrov, met in Baku, the capital of Azerbaijan, on Thursday, where they discussed “relations with the United States and the developments involving the Ukraine and Iran crises as well”, according to Moscow.
China did not...
title: Could Trump join Xi and Putin for 3-way meeting at next month’s Apec summit?

author: Caroline Lin
description:
Authorities in the central Chinese province of Hunan have warned of the potential risks of cross-border arranged marriages, saying some relationships lack genuine emotional foundations and can lead to financial ruin or legal trouble.
Marriages can be risky when they are organised by illegal matchmaking agencies that charge high fees, according to a post on the Xintian county police branch’s social media account on Tuesday.
For-profit international matchmaking is illegal in China.
The post...
title: Cross-border matchmaking can lead to financial ruin, Chinese police warn rural men

author: Liu Zhen,Carol Yang
description:
A grassland fire in Mongolia has raised fresh concerns in China, underscoring the recurring risk of cross-border environmental hazards.
This is not the first time an environmental disaster originating in Mongolia has threatened to cross the 4,700km (2,920-mile) border into China, with the impacts sometimes also affecting the Korean peninsula and Japan.

The blaze, which erupted on October 8 in the inland country’s easternmost Dornod province bordering Russia and China, advanced rapidly towards...
title: Vehicle may have sparked Mongolia wildfire, putting China rescuers on high alert

author: Finbarr Bermingham
description:
The EU’s surprise deal with China on hybrid cars last week was supposed to ease the pressure on Beijing. Instead, Brussels is preparing to intensify its crackdown on Chinese trade practices, emboldened by the discovery that its threats are finally delivering results.
Now, those driving trade policy for the bloc believe they have landed on a two-track formula. Intensive dialogue is seen to have yielded results and will continue.
But so too will the European Union’s efforts to counter what they...
title: Emboldened by hybrid car deal, Europe coalesces around tougher China stance

author: Phoebe Zhang
description:
As the Chinese saying goes, “Even an upright judge finds it hard to settle family matters.” Whenever Chinese TV channels air reality shows that centre on couples or parent-child relationships, controversy is guaranteed.
Heated debates ensue over who is right and who is wrong. Viewers examine every facial expression in microscopic detail and overanalyse every word before arriving at their verdict.
Yet, that wasn’t the case with Zhang Jiaqi after the Olympic diving medallist and her mother, Xiao...
title: Young Chinese are choosing healthy relationships over toxic filial piety

author: Nayan Seth,Khushboo Razdan
description:
The United States and China are in regular talks to iron out details of a framework announced last month for handling AI-related incidents and institutionalising bilateral dialogue, multiple sources told the South China Morning Post.
The technical teams of the two countries aim to make AI cooperation a potential deliverable when presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in Shenzhen next month – their third face-to-face...
title: US and China race to shape AI agenda ahead of Xi-Trump talks in Shenzhen, sources say

author: Chao Kong
description:
Chinese military scientists claim they have developed an algorithm that could help identify electronic warfare units using civil aviation flight data.
The researchers said they had located two sources of interference that were spoofing their locations near Israel during the conflict with Iran.
The team did not explain why they had focused on the Israeli military.
The researchers estimated the locations of the two units as being near Haifa, with reported positioning errors between 10.9km and...
title: Chinese scientists use open-source data to spot suspected Israeli electronic warfare units
